chunks: The takbir during the Days of Tashriq.

The takbir in Eid al-Adha is from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer of the fourth day; that is in fifteen prayers, and that is in Mina. In the towns, it is after ten prayers, from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer of the third day. The takbir is that you say:

Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. Allah is the Greatest for what He guided us to, and praise belongs to Allah for what He has bestowed upon us, and Allah is the Greatest for what He provided us from the cattle of the grazing livestock.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ ٱلتَّشْرِيقِ: The days following Eid al-Adha in which this takbir is recited.
key_terms.بَهِيمَةِ ٱلْأَنْعَامِ: The sacrificial livestock provided by Allah.
key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina, where the takbir continues for a longer number of prayers.
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلنَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice, the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.
key_terms.ٱلتَّكْبِيرُ: The prescribed recitation of declaring Allah's greatness after the prayers.
key_terms.ٱلْأَمْصَارِ: The towns or locations other than Mina.

ai.seo_question: What is the takbir recited after the prayers during the days of Tashriq, and how long is it recited?
ai.summary: This passage states the ruling for reciting the takbir after the salat during the days of Tashriq in Eid al-Adha, distinguishing between those in Mina and those in other towns. It also preserves the specific formula of takbir, expressing tawhid, praise, gratitude, and acknowledgment of Allah’s provision.
